15/14.03.2024 Learned counsel for the parties are present.

2. This revision application has been filed for appropriate order / orders, direction/direction to set
aside the Judgment dated 02-04-2019 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 28/2017 by the learned
Principal District and Session Judge.

Pakur whereby and whereunder the learned Principal District
and Session Judge, Pakur has been pleased to affirm the Judgment of Conviction dated 11-09-2017
u/s 498A of the I.P.C. and u/s 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 passed in G.R. No. 530/13
(Hiranpur P.S. case No. 71/13) by the learned Court of Sri Rakesh Ranjan, J.M. 1" Class, Pakur.

The
learned Principal District and Session Judge, Pakur further has been pleased to set aside the order
of sentences passed by the learned J.M. 1 Class, Pakur and case record is remanded back to the
Court of Learned J.M. 1 Class, Pakur with a direction to call for a report from the Probation officer
to consider the character of accused /appellant and thereafter to pass the sentences against him
according to provision of law.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has been convicted by the
learned Judicial Magistrate, 1 st Class, Pakur in connection with G.R. Case No. 530 of 2013
corresponding to T.R. No. 292 of 2017 vide order dated 11.09.2017 for the offence under Section
498-A of Indian Penal Code to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years with fine of
Rs. 1,000/- and under section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act

and has been sentenced to undergo

sentences.text:
rigorous imprisonment for one year and also to pay a fine of Rs. 1,000/-.
4.

He submits that the appeal against order of conviction has been dismissed vide order dated
2.04.2019 but so far as sentence is concerned the matter has been remanded to the court of learned
Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Pakur to call for a report from the probation officer to consider the
character of the accused/appellant and thereafter pass sentences against him according to the
provision of law.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that no fresh order has been
passed with regard to the sentence pursuant to the order dated 2.04.2019 and the present revision
application was filed which is pending since 2019.
5.

Learned counsel for the parties have submitted that a joint compromise petition has been filed
wherein it has been stated the petitioner and the informant have settled their dispute and are living
together.
They have also submitted that a child has also been born in the meantime.

They refer to
the order dated 29.09.2023 wherein counsel for both the parties had submitted that both are parties
are living together and, in the meantime, child has been born out of the wedlock two months prior to
29.09.2023.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that in view of the compromise entered into
between the parties, present case be disposed of in terms of the compromise.

The petitioner
remained in custody during the period from 16.01.2022 and provisional bail was granted by this
Court only on 19.10.2022 and a few days must have been taken by the petitioner in furnishing the
bail bond.
The provisional bail is expiring on 31st of March 2024.

7. The learned counsel for the State has submitted that he has no objection particularly considering
the fact that the petitioner and informant are living together peacefully and a child has been born in
the meantime.
8.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of
this case this Court has gone through the joint compromise petition being I.A. No. 8596 of 2022 and
the order sheet of this court which reflects that the parties have settled their dispute outside of the
Court and are living together peacefully and a child has been born in the meantime.

In such
circumstances in order to secure the ends of justice between the parties so that the parties may
continue to live peaceful conjugal life, this revision application is disposed of in terms of the
compromise between the parties.
I.A. No. 8596 of 2022 is allowed.
9. Consequently, the Judgment dated 02-04-2019 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 28/201
7 by the learned Principal District and Session Judge.
Pakur affirming the Judgment of Conviction dated 11- 09-2017 passed in G.R. No. 530/13 (Hiranpur P.S. case No. 71/13) by the learned Court of Sri Rakesh Ranjan, J.M. 1" Class, Pakur are set aside.
10. The petitioner is discharged from the liability under the bail bond furnished by him.
11. Let this order be communicated to the court concerned through FAX.
